title: State v. Mohit Kumar
text: The State of Delhi challenges the acquittal of the accused, Mohit Kumar, in a murder trial. The Sessions Court acquitted the accused primarily on the ground that the eyewitnesses were related to the deceased and hence unreliable. The High Court notes that relationship is not a ground per se to discard testimony of witnesses. The injured eyewitness gave a cogent and consistent account. The circumstantial evidence including the discovery of the weapon at the accused's instance also corroborates the prosecution case. The High Court reverses the acquittal and convicts the accused under Section 302 IPC. Considering the nature of the crime and lack of provocation, the sentence is life imprisonment with fine. The complainant's family is entitled to victim compensation under the scheme.
